propositions: Accepted /rerun and recheck-review requests exist only as in-memory _rebar_force events and are lost if the process exits before the event is dequeued, leaving the revision with a stale nonzero Gerrit vote and matching SQLite voted row so reconciliation skips it.

The repair requires reset-first durability: accepted requests must reset the exact revision to neutral LLM-Review: 0, verify no nonzero vote survives, and only then reset budget and enqueue the forced event; the reset-emitted comment-added event carrying patchSet.revision and patchSet.ref is the durable marker.

Reconciliation must query Gerrit before local dedup; a confirmed no-nonzero-vote read clears only the exact stale voted row and proceeds to vote, while Gerrit read errors preserve dedup and hold the cursor back for retry.

Contributor requests and malformed events cannot select label values or mint PASS/BLOCK; only the privileged reset operation writes a fixed neutral value 0, and affirmative/refusal replies remain label-free.
Reset/verify failure must reject the request, emit appropriate warnings, and leave the attempt budget and dedup unchanged; concurrent or admin votes are fail-closed and prevent acceptance.

A held-out restart test with old nonzero vote, matching stale dedup, exhausted budget, and advanced cursor proves that process loss followed by one reconcile pass recovers via the Gerrit-emitted event, casts exactly one new vote, and preserves unrelated dedup state.
